page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard4.Ax.Flex.4-32 is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration based on Intel x86_64 architecture. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 6987C-P processor operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. It features 4 dedicated physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled at two threads per core, yielding 8 virtual central processing units (vCPUs). System memory is configured at 32.0 GB, providing an even 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU (8.0 GB per physical core).

This instance configuration includes no dedicated hardware acceleration, with zero GPUs provisioned. Local storage is not attached directly to the host, meaning persistent and non-persistent storage must be mounted via network-attached block volumes. Networking features include one complimentary public IPv4 address for external routing and connectivity.

The 1:4 core-to-memory ratio characterizes this shape as a balanced compute option. By pairing a high 3.9 GHz base CPU frequency with dedicated execution threads, it offers consistent execution times without thread contention from neighboring tenants. Because local NVMe storage is absent, primary system performance is tied directly to network storage performance for input-output heavy workloads.

VM.Standard4.Ax.Flex.4-32 delivers a cost-efficient profile for moderate multi-threaded tasks that do not demand expansive local drive caches or specialized accelerator hardware. Primary workload fits include enterprise web application serving, software build pipelines, intermediate caching layers, microservices clusters, and light-to-moderate database instances operating with attached network storage.

It is equipped with an Intel Xeon 6987C-P processor operating at 3.9 GHz, delivering 4 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs through two-way multithreading. System memory totals 32.0 GB, maintaining a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The server has no integrated GPUs and includes no local physical storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for file systems and data persistence. Connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. With dedicated core assignment and high processor frequency, this instance provides predictable compute capacity without hypervisor thread contention. It is well suited for web serving, microservices architectures, build environments, and enterprise applications requiring reliable single-thread and multi-threaded throughput.
